subtype: Approach: leaving and telling an adult when boundaries are crossed [Action]
passage: Sit down, jaan, and listen to your Afreen Khala. At fifteen, a boy in my class, Akash, kept poking my shoulder and pulling my dupatta, and each time I said stop, he laughed. It went on for two weeks. Then I did what I wish I had done on day one. The next time, I said “Stop” once, loudly, and walked away without looking back. I went straight to Mrs Dsouza, our class teacher, and told her everything. She put a hand on my shoulder, said it was not my fault, and took me to the principal that same afternoon. That evening I told Ammi and Abbu, and Ammi sat beside me while I wrote down every date I could remember. I was shaking, but nobody doubted me. You say stop, you walk away, you tell.

qa.q: Who did Afreen go to straight after walking away?
qa.a: Afreen went straight to Mrs Dsouza, the class teacher.

qa.q: How did Afreen feel through it, and what shows it?
qa.a: Afreen felt frightened but relieved to be believed, since she was shaking yet nobody doubted her.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story, and why did it work?
qa.a: Saying stop once, loudly, walking away and telling adults was the turning point, because it stopped putting up with it and brought help the same day.

qa.q: How might Ammi have felt sitting beside Afreen?
qa.a: Ammi was probably worried and protective but supportive, since she sat beside Afreen while the dates were written down.

grounding: When a classmate repeatedly touches her after being told to stop, a teen walks away, tells a teacher and her parents and notes dates.

subtype: Approach: leaving and telling an adult when boundaries are crossed [Action]
passage: It happened again in the lab queue on Monday: a hand on Manjula's shoulder, sliding down her back. "Stop it, Sunil," she said, loud enough for others to hear. He laughed. It was the third time since Thursday. Manjula stepped out of the line and walked into the corridor, Parveen right behind her. Their class teacher was on leave all week, and unit tests started the next day. "Just wait till she's back," Parveen whispered. Manjula shook her head. In the back of her diary she had already written: Thursday, library. Friday, bus line. Monday, lab queue. She went to the vice principal's office instead. Mrs. Bhatt read the three lines, thanked her, called the school counsellor, and phoned Manjula's parents before lunch. That evening Amma and Appa sat with Manjula for a long time, and Sunil had been called in that same afternoon.

qa.q: What had Manjula written in the back of her diary?
qa.a: Thursday, library. Friday, bus line. Monday, lab queue.

qa.q: Why did Manjula refuse to wait until the class teacher returned?
qa.a: Manjula felt fed up and determined after the third time, and did not want it to go on while she waited.

qa.q: What else could Manjula do if it happens again?
qa.a: Manjula could add the date to her notes right away and report it straight to Mrs. Bhatt or the counsellor the same day.

qa.q: How might Parveen see Manjula's choice?
qa.a: Parveen first thought waiting was easier, but watching Manjula act at once may show Parveen that a report does not have to wait for one particular teacher.

grounding: Shows a teen who is touched again after saying stop walking away, reporting to a senior teacher and her parents, and keeping dated notes.

subtype: Approach: leaving and telling an adult when boundaries are crossed [Action]
passage: On the school bus in Hyderabad, Nilesh kept "accidentally" leaning into Sangeeta and resting his hand on her knee. On Tuesday she pushed it off. "Don't touch me." On Wednesday she said it again, louder. On Friday, when his hand came back, she stood up mid-ride, moved to the seat behind the driver beside the bus attendant, and stayed there until school. Before first period she opened her notes and typed: Tue, Wed, Fri, bus, hand on knee, told him to stop each time. Then she walked into the staffroom and asked for Mr. Qureshi, her class teacher. He listened without interrupting, told her she had done the right thing, and took her straight to the counsellor. By evening her parents had met both of them, and Nilesh had been moved to another bus.

qa.q: Where did Sangeeta move to on Friday?
qa.a: She moved to the seat behind the driver beside the bus attendant.

qa.q: What does Sangeeta's standing up mid-ride suggest about how she felt?
qa.a: Sangeeta was angry and fed up after saying stop twice, and determined not to stay beside Nilesh any longer.

qa.q: What else could Sangeeta have done after the first time on Tuesday?
qa.a: She could have told the bus attendant or a teacher right away, so adults were watching from the start.

qa.q: How does Mr. Qureshi see Sangeeta's report?
qa.a: Mr. Qureshi takes it seriously, listening fully, telling her she did the right thing and bringing in the counsellor that same morning.

grounding: Illustrates a teen walking away from a classmate who keeps touching her after being told to stop, noting the dates and reporting to her teacher and parents.
